sections.title: Belief, action, and secular ethics
sections.rationale: This exchange establishes whether conduct requires religious belief and whether contemplative practice can independently ground ethical behavior.

sections.title: Religious stories and cultural evolution
sections.rationale: This section tests whether inherited stories embody indispensable archetypal knowledge or remain culturally transmitted and contestable constructions.

sections.title: Secular societies and inherited morality
sections.rationale: The speakers directly contest empirical social outcomes and whether modern moral institutions remain dependent on religious inheritance.

sections.title: Tragedy, meaninglessness, and purposive action
sections.rationale: This exchange tests whether meaning must withstand tragedy and whether accepting ultimate meaninglessness can coexist with ordinary purposive action.

sections.title: Constructed higher meaning and the God-function
sections.rationale: The closing exchange contests whether culturally constructed higher meanings remain secular or necessarily perform the functional role of God.
